title: The part of the fibre over V(I) finite over A/I comes from the integral closure
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $A\to B$ a ring map of finite type ($B$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra). Suppose $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ is a product of $A/I$-algebras with $C_1$ finite over $A/I$ (a finitely generated $A/I$-module); let $\varepsilon\in B/IB$ be the idempotent $(1,0)$. Let $B'\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$ (the subring of elements of $B$ that are roots of monic polynomials with coefficients in the image of $A$). Then there are an idempotent $\varepsilon'\in B'/IB'$ and an element $g\in B'$ such that: (i) the ring map $B'/IB'\to B/IB$ induced by the inclusion $B'\subseteq B$ maps $\varepsilon'$ to $\varepsilon$, so that, writing $B'/IB'=C'_1\times C'_2$ with $C'_1=\varepsilon'(B'/IB')$, $C'_2=(1-\varepsilon')(B'/IB')$, it maps $C'_1$ into $C_1$ and $C'_2$ into $C_2$; (ii) the induced map $C'_1\to C_1$ is an isomorphism; (iii) the image of $g$ in $B'/IB'$ is $\varepsilon'$; (iv) the map of localizations $B'_g\to B_g$ induced by the inclusion is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$. Looking at the fibre rings, the finite $A/I$-algebra $C_1$ makes $A\to B$ quasi-finite at every prime in $T$.

source.place: :2512-2516, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH; affine quasi-finite definition/criteria are Algebra Tags 00PL, 00PK, 00PM

proof.text: Write $\phi:\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ for the map induced by $B'\subseteq B$. For each prime $\mathfrak p\in T$, Zariski's Main Theorem gives $h_{\mathfrak p}\in B'$ outside $\mathfrak p$ for which $B'_{h_{\mathfrak p}}\to B_{h_{\mathfrak p}}$ is an isomorphism. The union $U=\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in T}D(h_{\mathfrak p})$ is open, contains $T$ in its inverse image, and $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a homeomorphism with isomorphic local rings. In Lean, choose these elements as a family indexed by T. Mathlib SpecMapRestrictBasicOpenIso identifies each restricted spectrum map with the spectrum map of awayMap; isIso_SpecMap_iff turns bijectivity into an isomorphism. The open cover of the supremum, Opens.iSupOpenCover, and IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.iff_of_openCover glue the isomorphisms. Membership in the union follows from the element being outside the prime. This is the fully proved private helper exists_isIso_neighborhood_of_awayMap_bijective.

source.place: :2517-2531, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH, diagram and paragraph invoking Algebra Theorem Tag 00Q9

proof.text: The subset $T$ is open in the closed fibre over $V(I)$. Transporting this open subset through the homeomorphism over $U$ makes $\phi(T)$ open in the closed fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}(B')$. Since $C_1$ is finite over $A/I$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is finite and its image is closed; hence $\phi(T)$ is open and closed. The clopen decomposition and the inverse-image calculation give $B'/IB'=C'_1\times C'_2$, with $C'_1\to C_1$ an isomorphism and the two factors mapping into $C_1$ and $C_2$ respectively.

source.place: :2529-2541, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH; Algebra Tags 00HZ (going-up-closed), 00GU (integral going-up), and 00EE (disjoint clopen product)

proof.text: Let $\varepsilon'\in B'/IB'$ be the idempotent $(1,0)$ for this product decomposition. Because $\operatorname{Spec}(C'_1)$ is contained in $U$, choose $g\in B'$ mapping to $\varepsilon'$ with $D(g)\subseteq U$; the same open-and-local-ring comparison gives $B'_g\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g$. To apply the existing Lean choose-g interface, give each product factor its A/I-algebra structure by composing the quotient ring map A/I -> B'/IB' with the product equivalence and the appropriate projection. Compatibility of the quotient comparison with algebraMap proves that the factor maps commute with A/I. A prime of the first factor pulls back to a prime omitting the idempotent; the image identity from the image-clopen lemma therefore places it in U.

source.place: :2542-2549, proof of Lemma Tag 09XH; Algebra Tags 00EE (product) and 00E9 (local criterion)

proof.text: The product idempotent has image $(1,0)$ in $C'_1\times C'_2$, so the decomposition in the preceding steps is exactly the decomposition required in (i)--(ii), while the chosen $g$ gives (iii)--(iv). Explicitly, for c in C_1 take the inverse under the product equivalence of (f_1^{-1}(c),0), where f_1 is the first-factor ring equivalence. Multiplication by the idempotent fixes this element and its image is (c,0). Conversely, a fixed element has second coordinate zero; the equation for its image determines its first coordinate by injectivity of f_1. The same coordinate calculation for the complementary idempotent proves preservation of the second factor. The supplied epsilon equals the inverse image of (1,0) by injectivity of e.
